title: Just by meeting, Quad leaders send a signal to Beijing | The Strategist
paragraphs: China’s longstanding opposition to the Quad, and its concern with this week’s meeting of the group’s leaders in Manila, heightens the importance of the summit’s political signal.

The leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the United States didn’t hold a 2025 Quad meeting, so this will be the first between the group’s heads of government since 2024. Whether the summit produces a substantive new outcome is less of an issue than the political signal they send to the region and above all China by coming together.

The Quad partners share a basic unity of purpose: to support Indo-Pacific nations strengthening their sovereignty and to constrain China’s attempts to undermine it. With China seeking to take advantage of US focus on Iran, this Quad summit will likely make clear that all four members treat Indo-Pacific stability as their top priority. The summit will also debunk several false claims and comparisons.
